nodes.summary: For every complex number $z$, let $[z]$ be the Gaussian integer nearest to $z$, obtained by rounding the real and imaginary parts to the nearest integer with halves rounded up. Then $|\operatorname{Re}(z - [z])| \le 1/2$ and $|\operatorname{Im}(z - [z])| \le 1/2$.
nodes.title: Rounding error of the nearest Gaussian integer

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number with Hurwitz iterates $z_0 = z, z_1, z_2, \dots$. For $n \ge 0$, the $n$-th partial quotient is $a_n = [z_n]$, the Gaussian integer nearest to $z_n$, obtained by rounding the real and imaginary parts of $z_n$ to the nearest integer with halves rounded up.
nodes.title: Partial quotients of the Hurwitz expansion

nodes.summary: Let $w$, $x$, $y$ be natural numbers such that $w$ is odd and not a perfect square, $2x < w$, $2y < w$ and $w$ divides $x^2 + y^2 + 1$. Expand $z = (x + yi)/w$ by the Hurwitz algorithm, with convergent numerators $P_n$ and convergent denominators $Q_n$. Then there is exactly one natural number $n$ such that $n + 1$ is a legal index for $z$, $|Q_n| \le \sqrt{w} < |Q_{n+1}|$, and, if $|Q_n| \ne \sqrt{w}$,…
nodes.title: Sums of four squares via Hurwitz continued fractions

nodes.summary: For a complex number $z$, the Hurwitz iterates are $z_0 = z$ and $z_{n+1} = (z_n - [z_n])^{-1}$ for $n \ge 0$, where $[u]$ is the Gaussian integer nearest to $u$, obtained by rounding the real and imaginary parts of $u$ to the nearest integer with halves rounded up, and where the inverse of $0$ is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: Iterates of the Hurwitz algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number with Hurwitz iterates $z_j$ and partial quotients $a_j$. A natural number $n$ is a legal index for $z$ when $z_j \ne a_j$ for every $j < n$, that is, when the Hurwitz expansion of $z$ has not terminated before step $n$.
nodes.title: Legal indices of the Hurwitz expansion

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number with Hurwitz partial quotients $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$. Its convergent numerators $P_n$, $n \ge 0$, are given by $P_{-1} = 1$, $P_0 = a_0$ and $P_{n+1} = a_{n+1} P_n + P_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Convergent numerators of the Hurwitz expansion

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number with Hurwitz partial quotients $a_n$, convergent numerators $P_n$ and convergent denominators $Q_n$. Then $P_0 = a_0$, $Q_0 = 1$, $P_1 = a_1 a_0 + 1$ and $Q_1 = a_1$, and for every $n \ge 0$, $P_{n+2} = a_{n+2} P_{n+1} + P_n$ and $Q_{n+2} = a_{n+2} Q_{n+1} + Q_n$.
nodes.title: Recursion for the Hurwitz convergents

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number with Hurwitz partial quotients $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$. This is the sequence whose term for $n \ge 0$ is the pair of pairs of complex numbers $((P_{n-1}, Q_{n-1}), (P_n, Q_n))$, where $P_{-1} = 1$, $Q_{-1} = 0$, $P_0 = a_0$, $Q_0 = 1$, and $P_{n+1} = a_{n+1} P_n + P_{n-1}$ and $Q_{n+1} = a_{n+1} Q_n + Q_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Consecutive pairs of Hurwitz convergents

nodes.title: Error of the Hurwitz convergents

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number with Hurwitz partial quotients $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$. Its convergent denominators $Q_n$, $n \ge 0$, are given by $Q_{-1} = 0$, $Q_0 = 1$ and $Q_{n+1} = a_{n+1} Q_n + Q_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Convergent denominators of the Hurwitz expansion

nodes.summary: For a complex number $z$, let $[z] = m + n i$, where $m = \lfloor \operatorname{Re} z + 1/2 \rfloor$ and $n = \lfloor \operatorname{Im} z + 1/2 \rfloor$; that is, the real and imaginary parts of $z$ are rounded to the nearest integer, with halves rounded up. Then $[z]$ is a Gaussian integer nearest to $z$.
nodes.title: Hurwitz rounding to the nearest Gaussian integer

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number and let $Q_0, Q_1, \dots$ be the convergent denominators of its Hurwitz continued fraction expansion. For every $n \ge 0$ such that $n + 1$ is a legal index for $z$ (the expansion has not terminated before step $n + 1$), $|Q_n| < |Q_{n+1}|$.
nodes.title: Hurwitz's theorem: the convergent denominators grow in absolute value

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number and let $P_k$ and $Q_k$ be the convergent numerators and denominators of its Hurwitz continued fraction expansion. For every legal index $k$ for $z$ (the expansion has not terminated before step $k$), $|z - P_k / Q_k| \le 1 / |Q_k|^2$.
